headline: Claude 全线故障抢走当日最大流量，AI 助手已从效率工具变成生产链路的单点风险

overview_bullets.text: claude.ai、Claude Code 与 platform.claude.com 同时报错并被顶上热榜前排，用户的第一反应不是换模型而是停工，说明单一供应商依赖已成既定事实。
Google 的 modern-web-guidance、Chrome DevTools MCP、阿里 open-code-review、OpenAI codex-security 同日上榜，竞争焦点从"模型会不会写"转向"工具链能不能管住它"。
PhysLoop、BirdDreams、Duo、WorldDraft 集中出现，视频生成的研究口径已从"画面像不像"切换为"物理与因果对不对"。
Open Vision Banana 把闭源视觉感知流程完整开源复现，说明追赶路径仍是"复刻配方"而非"另起范式"。
《No AI Slop》宣言与 Claude 宕机同榜，用户对生成内容的耐受度下降与对 AI 的依赖度上升，正同时发生。

executive_summary: 今天的新闻重心不在模型能力，而在可靠性、可管性与可信度——基础设施一宕机，整条 AI 叙事就得暂停。

editor_note.core: 今天最该记住的是 Claude 的这次全线报错，而不是任何一篇论文。它把"AI 已是生产基础设施"这句话从判断变成了事实：一旦 claude.ai、Claude Code 与 API 同时不可用，用户没有降级预案，只能停工等待——这意味着模型供应商的可用性 SLA 即将成为采购决策的第一顺位，能力强弱退居第二。
editor_note.cross_signal: 三个信号互相咬合：一是 Claude 故障霸榜，二是开源热榜被 Google、阿里、OpenAI 的"代码审查/漏洞修复/浏览器规范"工具占满，三是论文侧集体转向世界模型的可靠性与决策可靠性（SO-Arena、Actor/Judge/Teacher）。三者指向同一件事——行业瓶颈已从"能不能做出来"转到"能不能稳定、可控、可审计地跑下去"。
editor_note.counterintuitive: 热度最高的开源项目几乎全是大厂内部工具的对外发布，所谓"开源生态繁荣"实质是闭源公司在下游铺设接口；而真正方法层面的开放（Open Vision Banana 的全配方复现）热度只有前者一半。开源的声量和开源的价值，正在系统性错位。
editor_note.risk: 最值得警惕的盲点是"配方复现幻觉"：Ropedia 那篇直接引用 GPT-6 Astra、Claude Fable 5.1 这类未见公开依据的模型名，说明部分论文的能力叙事跑在可验证事实之前。若这类引用被当作基准传播，后续工作的对比结论会整体失真。

contradictions: 同一时段既有"Claude Is Down"的故障抱怨，又有"Claude Meetings"的新功能讨论，故障与发布被混为一谈，社区信息噪音掩盖了真实可用性状况。
论文侧强调世界模型需要"可靠的质量判断与物理监督"，但部分工作引用的旗舰模型（GPT-6 Astra、Claude Fable 5.1）缺乏可核实来源，方法论严谨性与引用严谨性不一致。
社区一面高呼《No AI Slop》抵制 AI 生成内容，一面在 Claude 宕机时集体停摆，反 AI 的姿态与对 AI 的依赖直接对立。
underrated: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding（视觉编码器该不该保留的系统性拆解）
Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP（二阶优化器的显存与特征分解成本）
On the Design of Hyper-Connections（前沿模型已用但机制未明的架构组件）
tailscale/tailcat（绕开控制面的数据面工具，安全边界含义大于其热度）
block/buzz（蜂群式通信平台，组织协作形态的实验）

sections.name: 开源项目
sections.summary: 热榜被大厂出品的"智能体周边"占据：浏览器规范注入、DevTools 接口、代码审查、漏洞修复，开源正在变成闭源模型的能力延伸管道。

sections.name: 论文与研究
sections.summary: 十四条论文里近半指向世界模型与视频生成的可控性，另一半在啃优化器显存、视觉编码解耦等底层成本问题。

sections.name: 社区舆论
sections.summary: 抱怨宕机与呼吁"别再用 AI 生成垃圾"出现在同一张榜上，社区情绪从兴奋转向疲劳与问责。

sections.name: 产业与新闻
sections.summary: 平台级故障与全美机场地面停飞并列，两件事共同说明关键系统的单点失效代价正在被实时直播。

comments.one_liner: 一篇主张抵制 AI 生成的低质内容、呼吁保持作品人味的宣言式文章。
comments.why: 社区开始自己划线定义「低质 AI 产出」，把举证责任从读者转移到发布者身上，直接后果是平台需要给出可执行的标注与限流规则，而不是继续靠读者自行辨认。
comments.stance: 方向对，但宣言本身不具备执行力；真正的分水岭是社区是否愿意对熟人和大 V 同样开罚。

comments.one_liner: 名为 Claude Meetings 的项目，围绕 Claude 在会议场景中的使用展开。
comments.why: 会议记录是组织里敏感度最高的语料，助手一旦接进这一层，留存期限与访问权限就由模型厂商的默认设置决定，而不是由企业自己的合规策略决定。
comments.stance: 真正的产品价值在会后产出，不在实时旁听；先把数据留存条款谈清楚再谈功能。

comments.one_liner: 作者把旧金山湾区 1300 平方英里的 Google 逼真 3D 瓦片数据转制成可探索的像素风格等距地图。
comments.why: 个人开发者能把商用 3D 瓦片重新渲染成整座城市的风格化底图，说明高成本地理数据的下游再创作门槛已经降到单人可以完成的水平，随之而来的是衍生作品授权的灰色地带。
comments.stance: 地图本身好玩，真正的议题是商用瓦片的二次创作边界；这条边界不清，同类项目迟早会被叫停。

comments.one_liner: claude.ai、Claude Code 与 platform.claude.com 出现错误率升高的服务异常。
comments.why: 单一供应商的故障会同时切断所有下游团队的编码与调用链路，原本分散的风险被集中到一个状态页上，这会推动团队把多模型路由从备选方案变成默认架构。
comments.stance: 可用性已经变成采购指标而非加分项；故障通告的颗粒度和恢复说明应当写进合同，而不是靠事后发帖。

comments.one_liner: 美国所有机场当前处于全面停飞（ground stop）状态。
comments.why: 全国范围的停飞会在数小时内撞上机组执勤时限，真正的代价落在次日及第三天的排班恢复上，恢复期长度远超触发事件本身。
comments.stance: 全面停飞是当下唯一正确的粗暴手段，但航司对机组休息与运力回补的预案明显不足，这才是后续混乱的主因。

comments.one_liner: KORS 机场全频段的实时航空波段收听，Victoria, CA 同样处于停飞状态。
comments.why: 民间实时收听把原本封闭的航空管制频道变成公开的态势感知来源，在官方通报出来之前，公众已经能自行判断停飞范围，信息节奏从机构转移到个人。
comments.stance: 公开监听本身合理，但实时转播管制语音的边界要在事前定规矩，不能等出事后才补。

it_07479e65c6d5aa6e.title: SO-Arena: Benchmarking the Capability Spectrum and Reliability of System One Models
it_07479e65c6d5aa6e.summary: System One models promise fast, general-purpose decision-making without lengthy token generation. However, understanding their capability spectrum and decision reliability requires more than aggregate performance on current benchmarks. Existing evaluations often provide limited insight into the breadth of model capabilities and the reliability of their decisions. We introduce SO-Arena, a benchmark characterizing the capability spectrum and decision reliability of System One models across 11 domains and five capability families. For the capability spectrum, SO-Arena offers evidence-grounded evaluation through reliable sources and manual verification of reference labels against model-visible inputs; fine-grained capability assessment through domain-specific difficulty criteria; and realistic interactive evaluation, where models iteratively execute actions in sandboxes. Reasoning-intensive tasks further enable system one-two comparison. Beyond accuracy, SO-Arena assesses decision reliability through two complementary measures: decision stability under controlled option-set changes and missing-answer recognition when no valid option is available. Evaluations across 21 models reveal that the benefits of scaling and additional reasoning vary substantially across domains. More importantly, strong overall performance does not necessarily imply reliable decision-making: the best-performing System One model ranks only seventh in reliability. Together, these findings highlight the need to characterize capability spectrum and decision reliability as complementary dimensions, providing a systematic view of the strengths and limitations of System One models.

it_eb0a8524a4c84074.title: PhysLoop: Harnessing LLMs' Physics Awareness for Self-Improving Video Generation Models
it_eb0a8524a4c84074.summary: Video generation models produce visually realistic videos but still struggle with physical dynamics and causal consistency. Learning from generated videos requires fine-grained physical supervision, yet reliable quality judgments, correction pairs, and controlled variations are difficult to obtain. Large language models (LLMs) possess physical knowledge, but struggle to reliably guide video generation models in producing their training videos. We present PhysLoop, a unified harness designed to support physically grounded self-improvement in video generation models. The harness guides and constrains LLMs throughout video generation, selection, and correction, distilling their physical knowledge into physically consistent videos. The framework supports controllable training-data construction and inference-time video repair. By identifying and correcting failures, PhysLoop marks a key milestone toward recursive self-improvement (RSI) in video generation models with limited human intervention. We release 100K videos spanning diverse, realistic indoor and outdoor scenes, along with generation tools and two evaluation datasets: PhysLoop-Gen and PhysLoop-Repair. We evaluate controllable generation and localized repair on these datasets, respectively, and assess physical behavior on the external Physics-IQ Verified benchmark.

it_23fa06e2eaf60518.title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
it_23fa06e2eaf60518.summary: Decision models answer a question with a typed output, such as a choice among options with a probability for each, so one model can choose an agent's actions, evaluate actions already taken, or score every action to teach a policy with reinforcement learning. Prior work has studied them mainly as actors, judging their usefulness by how well they act. We ask whether a decision model that acts poorly can still teach well. We compare three decision models and three general LLMs as actors and judges on ALFWorld, and use JEV as a teacher on ALFWorld and WebShop. As actors, all six models are pulled away from a subgoal that must come first by an easier one. As judges that see the whole trajectory, the same models credit the steps toward that subgoal, and asking whether each action helped, rather than whether the task will succeed, separates useful from useless actions. As a teacher, JEV raises a Qwen2.5-1.5B policy over GRPO from 72.8% to 82.9% success on ALFWorld and from 56.8% to 71.4% on WebShop. These results suggest that a poor actor can still teach well, because judging an action after the episode ends reveals the consequences that acting must anticipate. Code is available at https://github.com/ZJU-REAL/decision-agents.

it_5f20605667d728f2.title: alibaba/open-code-review
it_5f20605667d728f2.summary: Secure, fast, efficient, battle-tested at Alibaba's scale. Hybrid architecture code review tool: deterministic pipelines + LLM Agent, precise line-level comments, built-in multi-language ruleset (NPE, thread-safety, XSS, SQL injection), OpenAI & Anthropic compatible.

it_42e3c8910f530bf1.title: BirdDreams: Joint Perspective and BEV Video Generation for a Plausible, Reactive Driving World Model
it_42e3c8910f530bf1.summary: Driving world models aim to simulate how a scene unfolds under different ego actions. This requires plausible motion of surrounding vehicles as well as precise ego-trajectory control. Learning vehicle motion from perspective video alone is challenging because motion is entangled with appearance and vehicles can be occluded. Prior work therefore conditions video generation on layouts that specify vehicle motion, providing control over surrounding vehicles but requiring their future trajectories as inputs. We introduce BirdDreams, an autoregressive driving world model that jointly generates perspective video and a schematic bird's-eye-view (BEV) video, making scene layout part of the predicted future. The BEV, rendered from scene annotations for training, depicts roads and vehicles as simple shapes at a fixed metric scale, providing a top-down view of their positions and motion with reduced occlusion between vehicles. Perspective video, by contrast, retains scene details that the BEV omits, such as traffic signals and object appearance. Joint attention between two video diffusion transformers, one per stream, lets each stream inform the other during generation. The predicted BEV also provides a geometric interface for ego control: we translate and rotate its latest frame along an input ego trajectory and use the resulting frames as a soft condition that shows how the scene would appear to move if only the ego vehicle moved. At inference, BirdDreams generates both videos from a single camera image without requiring an HD map or vehicle-state inputs. On PhysicalAI-AV and nuScenes, BirdDreams follows input ego trajectories more faithfully than prior driving world models and generates more plausible ego motion without ego-action conditioning. Human evaluation shows that BirdDreams outperforms a perspective-only baseline in generating realistic surrounding-vehicle behavior.

it_44bab6d343816615.title: Ropedia Xperience 2: A Gold Standard for Scaling Physical AI Environments and Behaviors
it_44bab6d343816615.summary: Large foundation models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 have recently been shown to control robots directly from visual observations. They nevertheless remain brittle on long-horizon, contact-rich tasks in real-world environments. Further progress depends on two complementary resources: demonstrations of human behavior that supervise how tasks are performed, and interactive environments in which policies can be rolled out, evaluated, and improved in closed loop. Language models have advanced along well-characterized scaling laws; the corresponding question for physical AI is how capability scales with environments and behaviors, which first requires identifying which data to scale and how to produce and reuse such data continuously. To address this question, we introduce Ropedia Xperience 2, comprising 1,589 released metric-scale 3D scans and a collection of 4,230 egocentric recordings of 74 tasks (131 hours). We further show that each capture can be repurposed for robot learning: scenes are converted into physically interactive simulation environments, human motion is retargeted to whole-body robot trajectories, and additional robot behaviors are obtained through virtual teleoperation and automated long-horizon trajectory generation. We propose this joint capture of environments and behaviors as a gold standard for physical AI data collection, laying a data foundation for establishing scaling laws over environments and behaviors.

it_59a3d999fb949b0b.title: Duo: A Reciprocal World Model for Full-Duplex Interaction
it_59a3d999fb949b0b.summary: In this report, we introduce the Reciprocal World Model (RWM) and present Duo v1, a full-duplex world model that continuously perceives audiovisual inputs while responding to users in real time. The RWM treats intelligence and physical reality as equally fundamental to what constitutes a world. Existing world models largely focus on simulating the latter, leaving reasoning and decision-making as external controls rather than intrinsic parts of the world itself. In RWM, we identify two equally fundamental capabilities: Intent, which provides the cognition underlying world interactions, and Realization, which generates coherent audio-visual behavior. To realize this formulation, Duo v1 introduces three key technical designs: (1) Leveraging autoregressive modeling for continuous interaction reasoning and participation decisions, rather than restricting it to instruction understanding for diffusion models. (2) Constructing chunk-specific conditions and synchronize tokens across Intent and Realization on a unified timeline. Module-specific attention masks enforce causal dependencies both within and across chunks, preventing access to future inputs. (3) Mitigating distribution shift in both modules through dual rollout distillation, training on autoregressively generated Intent tokens and synthesized audiovisual histories from Realization. Both modules continuously perceive real-time audio, video, and text, enabling full-duplex interaction with spontaneous conversations and interruptions. Beyond conversation, users can share real objects, reshape virtual scenes, guide assistants, or play audiovisual games without mouse or keyboard controls. The release of Duo v1 makes our first step, with the next version coming soon. We look forward to broader exploration of this emerging field.

it_f6862927ae7c7c00.title: G-STAR: Group-Scaled Token Capacity for Deeply Compressed Autoregressive Generation
it_f6862927ae7c7c00.summary: Discrete autoregressive models offer a scalable framework for image generation. However, they face a fundamental trade-off: long token sequences preserve representation quality but slow generation, while aggressive spatial compression reduces representation capacity. Based on product quantization, we show that, under a fixed nominal information budget, group size should scale quadratically with the per-axis spatial compression factor. Building on this principle, we propose GSTAR, a spatial--group co-scaling framework that enables \(32\times\) and even effective \(64\times\) compression while preserving strong reconstruction, understanding, and generation performance. Since larger groups introduce intra-group dependencies that must be modeled efficiently, we analyze their impact on inference latency and generation quality and introduce a semi-autoregressive decoder that combines parallel feature computation with lightweight causal modeling. With these designs, our highly compressed models perform competitively with leading models across five representative text-to-image benchmarks (GenEval, DPG-Bench, PRISM, LongText-Bench, and Qwen-Image-Bench). At \(1024\times1024\) resolution, our model delivers a \(20\times\) speedup over prior discrete autoregressive models, generating each image in 2.5 seconds on a single NVIDIA H200. Together, these results show that highly compressed discrete representations can enable high-quality autoregressive generation at low latency.

it_fb20c3d982d323ce.title: Open Vision Banana: A Fully Open Recipe for Generative Visual Perception
it_fb20c3d982d323ce.summary: Recent work suggests that pretrained image generators encode real-world understanding beyond image synthesis. Vision Banana exploits this by framing vision tasks as conditional image editing. However, its data, weights, code, and implementation details are not public. We present Open Vision Banana (OVB), a fully open and reproducible recipe for converting pretrained generators into unified multi-task perception systems. Our analyses identify the design choices that matter most for generalization, including color encoding, prompt design, parameter adaptation, and task balancing. These choices interact, so individually helpful choices can hurt when combined with others. Starting from 4B and 9B parameter open-weight base models and using 2.1M-3.8M training pairs from public datasets, OVB surpasses Vision Banana's reported Cityscapes zero-shot performance (73.9 vs. 69.9 mIoU) and rivals state-of-the-art affine-invariant depth estimators. Its non-zero-shot variants come within five points of Vision Banana on referring and reasoning segmentation but remain further behind on instance segmentation. All models largely retain the base model's image-editing abilities. With legend ensembling, we introduce a test-time scaling method for generator-based perception. It segments an image under several class-color legends and fuses the results by majority vote, correcting unstable color-class bindings and improving mIoU by up to 8.7 points on Cityscapes and 15.0 points on COCO-Object without retraining. We release the dataset construction and processing pipeline, the training and evaluation code, as well as the final, intermediate, and ablation checkpoints. Project website: https://openvisionbanana.github.io

it_adfb2fa52392a36c.title: TTB: Test-time Baking for Efficient Rendering of Decoder-only View Synthesis Models
it_adfb2fa52392a36c.summary: Decoder-only Large View Synthesis Models (LVSMs) with KV-cache have recently achieved state-of-the-art quality by regressing novel views from neural networks without reconstructing 3D geometry, while Test-Time Training (TTT) layers save computation but sacrifice quality. We propose Test-Time Baking (TTB), a strategy that learns to bake global scene information from cross-view attention into a lightweight MLP, enabling fast and high-fidelity novel-view decoding. The first key is to repurpose the fast-weight MLP of TTT to learn the cross-view attention mapping explicitly from its input-output pairs, rather than replacing attention entirely, achieving the same rendering efficiency as TTT while delivering substantially higher quality. The second key addresses a modality misalignment between context prefilling and novel-view rendering: we disentangle context tokens into camera-only context rendering tokens to serve as TTB input, and context ground-truth tokens with image content to serve as the TTB mapping target, ensuring the baked MLPs are relieved of the modality generalization challenge between context and novel-view processing. Our method achieves up to **23x** rendering speedup with quality on par with the state-of-the-art across several benchmarks. Project page: https://test-time-baking.github.io

it_0c774f26b21a95ed.title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
it_0c774f26b21a95ed.summary: How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate. Most models use a pretrained vision encoder, while some recent recipes train the encoder from scratch with the language model or remove it entirely. Vision encoders bundle together three design choices: a visual prior from upstream pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and pre-fusion placement of that capacity (i.e., before the multimodal backbone). Because published models also differ in data, architecture, and compute, comparing them cannot isolate the effect of each choice. We disentangle these choices via a controlled framework where we pretrain all models from scratch on common data and compare them on visual question answering and language benchmarks at matched lifetime compute. We find that the visual prior is not necessary; an encoder trained jointly from scratch is on par with a pretrained one, without a separate training stage. What matters instead is dedicated vision capacity: an encoder-free model trails on visual understanding even when its backbone is enlarged by the encoder's parameter count. Yet that capacity need not precede multimodal fusion, as vision-only modules added in-fusion to early backbone layers perform comparably to a pre-fusion encoder and can lower time to first token. These results also hold across backbone sizes, when encoder pretraining is treated as free, and when starting from a pretrained language model. Overall, our findings favor dedicated vision capacity trained jointly with the backbone and placed early within it.

it_34d3f43cb54e51f0.title: WorldDraft: If Code Builds the World, Can Video Models Just Render It?
it_34d3f43cb54e51f0.summary: Multimodal coding agents decouple 4D world construction from visual generation, repurposing video models from world generators toward generative renderers. This division of labor raises a fundamental question: if code builds the world, can video models just render it? A reliable generative renderer hinges on two complementary criteria: (i) world preservation, retaining prescribed 4D kinematics and camera paths; and (ii) visual realization, persistently binding text-specified target attributes over time. To evaluate this capability, we introduce WorldDraft, a benchmark of 432 strictly paired test cases across 48 executable 4D world families spanning six dynamic challenge categories. Under a 3 times 3 factorial design, WorldDraft orthogonally crosses draft granularity (abstract proxy to previs) and appearance alignment (neutral to conflicting) under identical dynamics. Extensive evaluations across 12 representative models reveal that: (I) world preservation and visual realization remain in stark operational tension; (II) richer draft scaffolding anchors structure but paradoxically impairs appearance fidelity; and (III) conflicting source cues trigger severe source leakage (up to 64%), exposing fragile cross-modal disentanglement. To mitigate these bottlenecks, we propose WorldDraft-Primer, a plug-and-play visual prompting strategy that consistently improves both objectives across frozen video renderers. Together, WorldDraft and WorldDraft-Primer lay a foundation for bridging programmatic 4D simulation with video generation, advancing physically grounded generative rendering.

it_0e6e1cee78d9d0b2.title: On the Design of Hyper-Connections: Simplification, Stability, and Scalability
it_0e6e1cee78d9d0b2.summary: Hyper-Connections (HC) architectures are increasingly adopted in frontier language models, yet their components remain insufficiently understood and introduce non-negligible training overhead. In this work, we systematically study the HC architecture to understand its components and identify simpler, more efficient designs. We find that learned read/write gating without mixing and unconstrained mixing with fixed gates form two effective interaction groups: either alone achieves performance comparable to mHC. We also identify repeated access to the expanded residual state as a major source of training overhead, even without mixing. These findings lead to SimpleHC, which simplifies the architecture by removing residual mixing and simplifies execution through shared memory access, using the resulting additive structure and shared gate inputs. Layer-specific gates share a group-entry state, enabling batched reads and deferred writes; scalar corrections exactly preserve preceding sublayer output contributions. Our analyses support both the retained residual structure and the design of shared memory access. SimpleHC incurs only 2.4% extra end-to-end training time over a vanilla residual baseline at the largest tested scale. It maintains performance comparable to mHC when scaling from 15B to 30B MoE models, exhibits smoother gradient dynamics during standard training, and remains stable under stress. We hope SimpleHC will encourage a broader pursuit of simplicity in foundation model design, making performance gains more accessible and practical at scale.

it_f657e631b1087d7c.title: Factored One-sided Adam-Moment for Practical and Scalable SOAP
it_f657e631b1087d7c.summary: Second-order optimizers (e.g., Shampoo, SOAP) have emerged as compelling alternatives to Adam/AdamW and promise faster per-step convergence than AdamW in transformer training. However, they still remain costly in practice, and even SOAP still pays substantial optimizer-state memory and eigendecomposition overhead. We ask whether the benefits of SOAP can be retained at nearly the efficiency of AdamW. In this paper, we answer yes with a lightweight SOAP variant, Factored One-sided Adam-Moment (FOAM). The path to practical impact is twofold: first, FOAM employs input-only preconditioning, dropping the output-side Kronecker factor to reduce memory and remove one eigendecomposition. The Kronecker structure of the Hessian shows that this is exact for a diagonal output-side curvature and nearly lossless for a near-diagonal one, as we observe empirically. Second, FOAM replaces SOAP's dense rotated second moment with a factored Adam-moment estimator based on row-by-column statistics. Under the K-FAC Fisher assumption with a diagonal output curvature, this estimator exactly recovers SOAP's dense second moment, and we measure only a 15-20% K-FAC violation, with negligible effect on the update. Our empirical results support the claim that FOAM matches strong SOAP and Muon baselines in validation loss across scales of large language model (LLM) pre-training, uses half of SOAP's optimizer state, runs at Muon-class wall-clock time, and retains robustness across a three-fold learning-rate range. The results hold from 124M to 760M parameters, demonstrating that SOAP's gains need not require SOAP's cost. Code: https://github.com/naver-ai/foam

it_30af7e2cf94ebf59.title: UniSpark: Exploring Hybrid Attention for Multimodal Understanding and Generation
it_30af7e2cf94ebf59.summary: We present UniSpark-9B, a unified multimodal model that investigates hybrid attention for visual understanding and generation. Built on a Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts backbone with approximately 9B parameters in each branch, UniSpark combines full attention for explicit token interactions with GatedDeltaNet linear attention for compact context propagation. Autoregressive text prediction and visual flow matching jointly support visual question answering, text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and interleaved text-image prediction. In interleaved generation, noisy visual targets are isolated from subsequent predictions, while clean visual representations provide context for later outputs. A blockwise protocol enforces this distinction through attention masks in full-attention layers and recurrent-state retention rules in linear-attention layers. The selected training sources contain 159.7M generation samples, 213.4M understanding samples, and 624.8K interleaved sequences. A four-stage curriculum jointly trains multimodal understanding and visual generation, refining answer accuracy and instruction following while extending image synthesis to 2K. UniSpark scores 2470.3 on MME-S and 0.83 on GenEval. Qualitative examples further illustrate its capabilities in interleaved image generation, video synthesis, and video editing. Together, these results demonstrate that hybrid attention provides an effective backbone for unified multimodal understanding and generation.
